common_copy_failed: Could not copy. Select and copy it manually.
auth_description: Use your operator account to manage the proxy control plane.
canvas_list_description: Every proxy topology this control plane manages.
canvas_list_empty_description: Create a canvas to start describing a proxy topology.
canvas_create_description: Name the topology this canvas will describe.
canvas_edit_description: Both the name and the description are replaced.
canvas_delete_warning: Deleting {name} also deletes every subcanvas, server, pod, exit and edge in it. Workers keep serving their last configuration until they are stopped.
editor_empty_description: Add a server, give it pods, and drag from a pod to where its traffic should go.
editor_override_none: Leave empty to use the derived value.
editor_server_icon_hint: Empty shows the flag of the IPv4 address's country. flag:us shows a country flag, logo:tauri a brand logo; anything else falls back to the default icon.
editor_server_log_level_hint: The worker switches to it as soon as the config reaches it, without a restart.
editor_server_ipv6_hint: Only decides which address family a domain-name destination resolves to. It has no other effect today; leave it alone unless you need it.
editor_server_quic_hint: This server's side of every QUIC relay link. Brutal sends at exactly the up rate whatever the path does; the master pairs each link's two ends so nobody sends faster than the other end can receive. 0 = default.
editor_server_quic_windows_hint: Windows are optional: 0 derives the stream window from the down rate and leaves the connection window unlimited.
editor_agent_description: The guru-worker on this server: the version it runs and the version that is published for it.
editor_agent_not_published: No worker release is published yet (manage-tool agent publish).
editor_agent_no_base_url: Set agent_public_base_url in the orchestration configuration to render install commands.
editor_agent_install_description: Paste the command on the server as a user with sudo. It downloads the published guru-worker, verifies it, writes guru-worker@<unit>.service and starts it.
editor_agent_install_once: The key is shown only now. Regenerating later replaces it, and a worker still holding it is refused at its next reconnect.
editor_agent_install_replaces: This server already has a key. A new command replaces it: the worker running with the old key is refused at its next reconnect.
editor_agent_install_after: Settings travel in the environment, not on the command line; the key is still briefly visible in ps while the installer runs.
editor_agent_install_uninstall: To remove it later: sudo bash /opt/guru-worker-{unit}.uninstall.sh (stops the service and deletes this instance's binaries, configuration and state).
editor_agent_unit_hint: guru-worker@<name>.service on the host: lowercase letters, digits and dashes.
editor_agent_updating: Updating to v{version}… the worker picks it up at its next poll and restarts.
editor_server_address_none: No address yet: wait for the worker to register, or pin one.
editor_server_delete_description: {name} and its {count} pods are deleted. Rules on other servers that dial it keep their last configuration until they are redrawn.
editor_pod_delete_description: {name} stops listening on port {port}, and its edges are removed.
editor_narrow_description: This canvas is not supported on mobile devices with a narrow screen. Open it on a wider display.
editor_subcanvas_create_description: Creates a canvas drawn inside this one. It only organises the drawing: edges cross into and out of it freely.
health_description: How the workers serving this canvas are doing.
health_placeholder_description: Worker health for this canvas will appear here.
settings_description: The name and description of this canvas, and its removal.
settings_danger_description: Removes the canvas with every server, node, port and edge on it.
help_description: How to describe a proxy topology on the canvas.
help_usage_description: A canvas draws a graph of pods: each pod listens on a server, and edges lead its traffic on to other pods or to exits.
help_step_add_body: Add servers and exits from the menu in the top-left corner. Pods are added on a server, in its panel: a client pod is where traffic enters, a relay pod receives it from other pods.
help_step_edit_body: Click a card, a pod row or a bus to open its panel on the right; a bus's panel names every line in it by colour and lists its edges with their ids. Drag the divider to resize it; close it with the X.
help_step_connect_body: Drag from the blue handle on the right of a pod to a red one: a relay pod's row, an exit, a server's header (a new relay pod there) or a splitter (the pod joins it). Lines always run from blue to red. A pod with several ways on balances over them; its panel turns that into failover tiers and nested groups.
help_step_arrange_body: Drag cards to move them; their position is saved when you drop them. Splitters and aggregators are drawn from the routes, but where you put them is remembered too.
help_step_problems_body: The control plane checks the whole tree; its findings are listed in the bottom-left corner. Click one to open what it is about, going to its canvas first when it lives elsewhere in the tree.
help_step_subcanvas_body: A subcanvas is a canvas drawn inside another. Double-click it to go inside. Edges cross canvases freely: drop a connection on a subcanvas to pick a pod or exit inside it.
help_step_delete_body: Select cards or buses and press Delete, or use the delete button in a panel. What goes is shown first, checked by the control plane, and applied as one change.
help_keys_description: Shortcuts work while the canvas has focus, not while typing in the panel.
help_key_delete: Remove the selected cards and buses
help_key_multi_select: Add a card or bus to the selection
help_key_focus: Move focus to the next card
help_key_nudge: Nudge the selected cards by 5 pixels
help_key_nudge_fast: Nudge the selected cards by 20 pixels
help_key_pan: Pan the view, even over cards
management_description: Accounts, API keys and your own profile.
accounts_description: Operator accounts that can sign in to this dashboard.
accounts_create_description: The account can sign in immediately with this password.
accounts_password_hint: At least 8 characters. This dashboard enforces the minimum, the control plane does not.
accounts_delete_description: {email} loses access immediately. Their sessions and API keys are deleted with the account.
api_keys_description: Your personal keys. They authenticate workers only and cannot sign in to this dashboard.
api_keys_create_description: Name the worker or integration this key belongs to.
api_keys_secret_once: Copy this secret now. It is shown once and cannot be recovered.
api_keys_copy_failed: Could not copy the secret. Select and copy it manually.
api_keys_revoke_description: Anything authenticating with {name} stops working immediately.
api_keys_empty_description: Create a key to let a worker register with the control plane.
profile_description: The account you are signed in as.
profile_password_changed: Password changed. Sessions on other devices stay signed in.
issue_members_invalid: Members: 1 to 256, each with a unique name of at most 64 characters.
error_forbidden: Your role does not allow this.
error_internal: The dashboard server failed while handling this request.
error_unavailable: The control plane is briefly unreachable. Your session is still valid — try again in a moment.
error_cannot_modify_self: You cannot change your own account here.
error_last_admin: The last administrator cannot be removed.
error_conflict: The same thing was changed at the same time, so nothing was saved. Try again.
error_timeout: The control plane did not answer in time.
error_unimplemented: The control plane does not support this request. The dashboard and the control plane may be running different versions.
error_control_plane: The control plane failed while handling this request.
error_invalid_request: The server refused a request this page sent. This is a bug in the dashboard.
error_network: Cannot reach the dashboard server. Check your connection, or wait for the server to come back.
error_stale_app: Part of the dashboard could not be loaded: it may have been updated, or the connection dropped. Reload the page to continue.
error_client: This page hit an error it did not expect. This is a bug in the dashboard.
error_unknown_result: The control plane answered with a result this dashboard does not know ({code}).
error_stale_title: What is shown may be out of date
result_email_taken: That email is already in use.
editor_rollout_description: What the control plane wants, what it handed to the worker, and what the worker confirmed.
editor_rollout_derive_failed_hint: This canvas could not be turned into a config for this server, so nothing new was published to it.
editor_rollout_apply_failed_hint: The worker rejected the config it was handed and keeps running the last one it applied.
editor_rollout_waiting_hint: This server points at a listener these servers have to serve first; it converges once they do.
editor_rollout_invalid_pods_hint: Only these pods failed: the rest of this server's config was published normally, and each pod listed here keeps whatever listener shape it was already serving.
editor_rollout_toml_description: The TOML the control plane renders for this server, exactly as the worker receives it.
editor_rollout_forget_description: This declares {name} dead. Servers that depend on it may then switch away from listeners it might in fact still be serving, which can cut live traffic. The record rebuilds itself once the worker reports again.
editor_entry_tls_description: Clients connect with TLS, terminated on this pod. The certificate is issued from this config by the derivation pass and managed on the TLS page.
editor_entry_tls_sni_hint: The hostname this pod terminates; the certificate is requested for it. A leading `*.` requests a wildcard.
editor_entry_tls_provider_admin_only: Only an administrator can list DNS providers, so the stored one is shown by id.
editor_entry_tls_no_providers_hint: The ACME challenge is answered over DNS, so a provider has to be registered before TLS can be issued.
editor_entry_tls_domain_hint: The provider's own id for the zone the SNI lives in.
editor_entry_tls_domain_hint_cloudflare: The Cloudflare zone ID of the zone the SNI lives in.
editor_entry_tls_domain_hint_vercel: The Vercel domain the SNI lives under.
editor_entry_tls_acme_hint: Leave empty to use the installation default.
issue_sni_required: Enter the hostname TLS is terminated for.
issue_sni_too_long: A hostname is at most 253 characters.
issue_sni_invalid: Enter a hostname such as edge.example.com, optionally starting with `*.`.
issue_dns_provider_required: Choose the DNS provider that answers the ACME challenge.
issue_domain_id_required: Enter the provider's zone or domain id.
issue_acme_directory_invalid: An ACME directory is an https:// URL, or empty for the default.
tls_description: DNS providers and the ACME certificates derived from your entry nodes.
tls_admin_only_description: DNS providers and certificates can only be managed by an admin.
tls_providers_description: Credentials the control plane uses to answer the ACME DNS-01 challenge.
tls_providers_empty_description: Add a provider before an entry node can request a certificate.
tls_provider_kind_immutable: The provider kind cannot be changed after creation.
tls_provider_account_hint_cloudflare: Cloudflare does not use this: the zone id is set on the entry node's TLS config.
tls_provider_account_hint_vercel: Vercel team id. Leave empty for a personal account.
tls_provider_secret_hint_create: Stored write-only: the control plane never returns it again.
tls_provider_secret_hint_edit: Leave blank to keep the stored token.
tls_provider_create_description: Give the control plane an API token that may edit the zone's DNS records.
tls_provider_edit_description: Rename the provider or replace its API token.
tls_provider_delete_description: {name} and its stored API token are deleted. The control plane refuses while an entry node still references this provider.
tls_certificates_description: The dashboard never issues a certificate: a row appears once the derivation pass reads an entry node's TLS config.
tls_certificates_empty_description: Set a TLS config on an entry node; the next derivation pass creates its certificate.
tls_certificate_retry_hint: Clears a failure, or forces a renewal, so the next pass picks this certificate up.
tls_certificate_retried: {sni} is queued for the next renewal pass
tls_certificate_delete_description: Certificate rows are created by the derivation pass from an entry node's TLS config, so deleting {sni} is refused while an entry node still references the same SNI and ACME directory. Remove the entry node's TLS config first.
health_summary_reporting_hint: of {total} servers on this canvas, in this window
health_no_servers_description: Add a server in the editor and its workers will report here.
health_no_records_description: The worker sent nothing back — it is offline, or it has never registered.
health_no_pods_description: Nothing is deployed to this server on this canvas, so it reports no deployment events.
issue_health_window_invalid: Pick one of the offered time windows.
config_auth_description: How long an idle session stays valid before it is rejected. Sessions slide on each authenticated request.
config_orchestration_description: Derivation behaviour, health polling, ACME issuance and the relay-certificate refresh cadences.
config_restart_description: guru-master reads every configuration key once at startup, so a saved change only takes effect after it is restarted.
config_unseeded_description: This key has no row yet, so the editor is showing the defaults. Saving creates the row with exactly the text below.
config_rejected_title: The control plane rejected this document
issue_config_json_invalid: The document is not valid JSON.
issue_agent_unit_invalid: 1-32 lowercase letters, digits or dashes, starting with a letter or digit
editor_policy_balance_hint: Spreads connections over the members that are alive, in proportion to their weights.
editor_policy_failover_hint: Uses the first member that is alive, in order: each tier takes over when every tier before it is down.
editor_sticky_hint: The same client address keeps going to the same member while it is alive. Needs a pod that knows the client address: a relay pod, or a client pod that receives PROXY.
editor_pod_ingress_client_hint: Clients connect to this pod directly; no pod can lead into it.
editor_pod_ingress_relay_hint: Other pods relay to this pod, in this protocol: every pod leading here dials it the way it listens.
editor_pod_port_hint: Leave empty to let the control plane pick a free port between 40000 and 59999.
editor_pod_dialed_by_none: No pod leads here yet: a relay pod nothing leads into is not deployed.
editor_route_description: Every way on is one edge. A balance spreads connections over its members by weight, a failover uses the first member that is alive; either may hold the other. Tick members to nest them.
editor_route_none: This pod goes nowhere yet: a pod with no way on is not deployed.
editor_route_none_client: This pod goes nowhere yet. Add a way on here, or drag from its row on the canvas.
editor_route_dirty_hint: Save or reset the shape before adding or removing a way on.
editor_way_remove_description: The edge to {name} is removed and the route closes around the gap.
editor_dial_description: How this edge dials the pod it leads to. Empty uses the pod's advertised address and its port.
editor_destination_hint: host:port, where traffic leaves the fabric.
editor_exit_create_description: Where traffic leaves the fabric. Any number of pods may lead here.
editor_exit_delete_description: {name} is deleted with the {count} edges leading into it.
editor_splitter_add_member_hint: A member added here is added to every route the splitter stands for: a new relay pod per route when it lands on a server.
editor_splitter_delete_description: Every way on under this splitter is removed from the {count} routes it stands for.
editor_aggregator_description: Where buses from several servers meet. Nothing about it is stored: it keeps parallel lines readable.
editor_bus_lines_hint: Each coloured line is one rule: the traffic of one client pod, shown with the server it runs on.
editor_bus_delete_description: The {count} edges of this bus are removed from their routes.
editor_portal_description: Edges of this canvas lead into, or come from, what is listed here.
editor_refused_unknown: The control plane refused the change.
editor_edit_client_pod_dialed: A client pod cannot be led into: only relay pods accept traffic from other pods.
editor_edit_self_dial: A pod cannot lead into itself.
editor_remove_description: Everything selected goes in one change, with the edges that lead into and out of it.
editor_review_prune: Also remove relay pods left unreached
editor_review_prune_hint: A relay pod nothing leads into any more goes too, with the ways on out of it.
editor_review_refused: The control plane would refuse this
editor_review_ok: The control plane accepts this change.
editor_target_description: A relay pod that exists, an exit, or a new relay pod on a server.
editor_target_new_relay_description: A new relay pod on {server}, on a port the control plane picks.
editor_target_protocol_hint: The new pod listens this way, and every pod leading to it dials it this way.
